title: Revealing Hybrid Zero-Dynamics Structure in Reinforcement Learning Policies for Humanoid Locomotion
abstract: Existing velocity-tracking policies for humanoid robots typically rely on multiple heuristic reward terms, yet they can achieve stable and diverse gait behaviors. However, how these rewards induce stable closed-loop dynamics in contact-rich hybrid systems remains poorly understood. This work analyzes reinforcement learning locomotion policies from the perspective of hybrid zero dynamics (HZD). Using full-body trajectories generated by a policy over a wide range of locomotion commands, we learn low-dimensional latent coordinates for a reduced-order model through an encoder-decoder, without prescribing physics-based template coordinates such as the center of mass, inverted-pendulum states, or momentum. We further construct a command-conditioned latent dynamics model that captures both state evolution at the control frequency and step-to-step return dynamics. This process identifies a family of hybrid periodic orbits and their neighborhoods parameterized by locomotion commands. By analyzing orbit reconstruction, consistency across contact transitions, contraction of the latent Poincare map, and transverse attraction around the orbit neighborhoods, we reveal an approximately hybrid-invariant orbit structure implicitly formed by policies trained with heuristic rewards. Furthermore, the extracted hybrid orbits can be used as a unified orbit-based reward to replace multiple explicit multi-gait tracking rewards in the original training objective, indicating that these latent orbits retain the gait objectives and stability-related information encoded by the original rewards. Experiments on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 validate the framework as a tool for interpreting reinforcement learning locomotion policies and demonstrate that the extracted orbit structure can be reused in subsequent policy learning.
